A field with water running down paths
A garden with no records or mulch
questions.correctAnswer: A mulched sack garden with drip bottles and a watering rota
questions.explanation: This design saves space and water while organizing regular care.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a suitable food production project for limited water and space.

questions.prompt: Which decision best uses records from a garden where tomato yields dropped after repeated tomato planting?
options: Rotate with beans or maize and improve soil fertility
Remove all compost from the garden
questions.correctAnswer: Rotate with beans or maize and improve soil fertility
questions.explanation: Records can reveal patterns; rotating crops and improving soil can address pest, disease, or fertility problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Use production records to make crop management decisions.

questions.prompt: Which plan best manages a poultry project with rising feed costs and fewer eggs?
options: Review feed, health, housing, and egg records with the teacher
Keep birds in a damp dark room
questions.correctAnswer: Review feed, health, housing, and egg records with the teacher
questions.explanation: Records and observations help identify whether feeding, health, or housing may be affecting egg production.
questions.learningOutcome: Use animal records to investigate production problems.

questions.prompt: Which school lunch plan best uses local foods for a balanced meal?
options: Githeri with sukuma wiki and a fruit
questions.correctAnswer: Githeri with sukuma wiki and a fruit
questions.explanation: Githeri provides energy and protein, while sukuma wiki and fruit add protective nutrients.
questions.learningOutcome: Create balanced meals using locally available foods.

questions.prompt: Which plan best protects learners while making a compost heap?
options: Wear gloves, avoid sharp waste, wash hands, and work with teacher supervision
Use broken glass to make layers
questions.correctAnswer: Wear gloves, avoid sharp waste, wash hands, and work with teacher supervision
questions.explanation: Protective equipment, safe material selection, hygiene, and supervision reduce risk during compost work.
questions.learningOutcome: Create safety procedures for compost-making activities.

questions.prompt: Which project goal best supports both income and nutrition for a school club?
options: Grow fast-maturing vegetables, eat some in balanced meals, and sell surplus safely
Grow vegetables but let all harvest spoil
Spend all income without recording it
questions.correctAnswer: Grow fast-maturing vegetables, eat some in balanced meals, and sell surplus safely
questions.explanation: The plan supports food supply, healthy eating, safe marketing, and simple agribusiness learning.
questions.learningOutcome: Design agriculture projects that support nutrition and income.

questions.prompt: Create a one-week duty rota for caring for a school vegetable garden.
questions.correctAnswer: Learner should include daily groups or names, watering times, weeding or pest-checking tasks, tool safety, record keeping, and teacher supervision.
questions.explanation: A useful duty rota shares work fairly and makes sure the garden receives regular care.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a duty rota for routine care of a school garden.

questions.prompt: Plan a balanced supper using four local foods and explain the role of each food group.
questions.correctAnswer: Learner should name a meal such as ugali, beans, vegetables, and fruit, then explain energy-giving, body-building, and protective roles.
questions.explanation: Meal planning should show variety and connect each food to its work in the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Create balanced meal plans using locally available foods.

questions.prompt: Describe how to make and use compost safely in a school vegetable garden.
questions.correctAnswer: Learner should describe collecting organic waste, avoiding plastics and glass, layering materials, keeping the heap moist, turning it, allowing decomposition, and applying mature compost to soil.
questions.explanation: Safe composting turns organic waste into manure while avoiding harmful materials and unfinished compost.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe procedure for making and using compost manure.

questions.prompt: Create a poster message that teaches safe food handling from harvest to eating.
questions.correctAnswer: Learner should include messages about washing hands, using clean harvesting containers, cleaning vegetables, using clean utensils, cooking food well, covering food, and storing it safely.
questions.explanation: A strong poster links hygiene actions from the garden or market to the plate.
questions.learningOutcome: Create clear messages that promote safe food handling practices.
